_note: Hand-maintained override: upstream exercise id → the specific deltoid head the
exercise trains. Applied at ingestion to `primaryMuscle` only.
Why it exists. The dataset has one undifferentiated `delts` bucket (§5.4), so
the mapping table cannot produce front_delts or side_delts at all — a lateral
raise and an overhead press both come through as `delts`. That is fine for
search and for substitution, and it is NOT fine for M6's per-muscle volume: on
a Push/Pull/Legs split the question 'am I doing enough side delt work' cannot
be answered from one bucket, because pressing volume swamps it. This table is
how an exercise gets classified when that answer starts to matter.
It is deliberately empty. Filling it is a per-exercise judgement, worth making
only for the exercises actually in the owner's program, and that program does
not exist until M3. Anything left out stays `delts`, which is honest rather
than wrong.
Rules the build enforces:
- the id must exist in the catalogue, and its primaryMuscle must resolve to
`delts` — an override on anything else is a typo and fails the build;
- the value must be front_delts, side_delts or rear_delts;
- synergist and secondary muscles are NOT rewritten. A press whose primary
is front_delts still lists a generic `delts` synergist, because a single
head per exercise cannot describe both positions honestly.
